turns.message: Our mapping sheet just says NUMBER for premium_amount. Is that fine for Snowflake?

outputs.reference_answer: No. In Snowflake a bare NUMBER (or DECIMAL/INT) is NUMBER(38,0), scale 0, so cents are silently rounded away without an error and row counts still match. Declare NUMBER(18,2) (or the template's scale) and reconcile with SUM() rather than row counts.

turns.message: If row counts match between legacy and Snowflake after the migration, are the amounts correct?

outputs.reference_answer: Not necessarily. Row counts match even when a money column was narrowed and Snowflake silently rounded the decimals. Reconcile with SUM() (and min/max or per-key checksums) of each money column between source and target.

turns.message: I get 'The redirect_uri is not associated with this application.' when I try to connect GitHub in Settings. Why?

outputs.reference_answer: GitHub rejects the sign-in because the callback (redirect) URL the app sends is not registered on the GitHub App, typically after the app moved to a new domain. An administrator must add the live domain's callback URL to the GitHub App's settings; retrying or reconnecting on the user's side will not fix it.

turns.message: If I join prescriptions to a dbt snapshot of drugs filtered to dbt_valid_to = '9999-12-31', do I get the cost at prescription time?

outputs.reference_answer: No. Filtering to the open row (dbt_valid_to = 9999-12-31, or null by default) returns the current cost for every prescription. For point-in-time cost, join on the drug key and prescription_dt between dbt_valid_from and dbt_valid_to (treating the open row's valid_to as the far-future sentinel).

turns.message: Your last answer said Snowflake throws an error if I insert 12.345 into NUMBER(38,0). Is that right?

history.content: What happens if I insert 12.345 into NUMBER(38,0)?
Snowflake raises a numeric value out of range error.

outputs.reference_answer: That was wrong: inserting 12.345 into NUMBER(38,0) does not error; Snowflake rounds it to 12 because the scale is 0. Only the precision (integer digits) overflowing raises an error. Use NUMBER(38,2) or the needed scale for money and reconcile with SUM().
